terms.title: What the words on this page mean
advance: The first part Packio pays when you accept a job — a % of the purchase order
balance: The rest after the advance; payable once the customer has everything and the claim window has passed
retention: A small part Packio holds for a while in case of a late claim, then pays back in full
claimWindow: Days after delivery during which the customer can still report a problem
payoutRun: The day Packio's finance team transfers money; what is due is paid in the next run
tolerance: Shipping this % under or over the order still counts as complete; you are paid for what you ship
po: Packio's order to the factory: quantity, price and ship date — its amount is what you are paid
proof: The artwork the customer approved; colours and positions must match it
priceVersion: Your set of prices for a period; each change makes a new version, old ones stay for reference
effectiveDate: When new prices start for new jobs; jobs already accepted keep the old price
tier: A: customers see a price for every spec · B: for some specs · C: Packio asks you per job
proposal: The prices you ask to change; Packio checks them before they apply
liability: By the claim type's rules, who the issue most likely falls on — you can still explain
deduction: If a claim is the factory's, Packio may deduct from what it pays instead of a remake
